task: Add a ref-addressable page-model snapshot to tools/chrome-bridge: a new pageModel page action that walks the active tab's top-frame DOM via a MAIN-world-injected function and returns a compact, row-capped array of actionable/interactive elements, each with a stable queryable ref, role, name and a viewport bounding box {x,y,width,height}, so an MCP agent feeds the bbox center to the existing clickAt/hover without a CSP-fragile executeScript. DOM-only (no CDP/debugger, no new manifest permission), existing 16 page actions unchanged, top-frame only, single foundational slice of the broader claude-in-chrome replacement.

analysis.objective: Add a DOM-based, ref-addressable page-model snapshot to the standalone chrome-bridge extension that walks the active tab's actionable/interactive elements and returns a compact list of stable-ref/role/name/bounding-box rows, so an MCP agent can target clickAt/hover (and a follow-up type) from element coordinates without executeScript or raw-HTML scraping — a single coherent slice of the long-term Chrome-control tool, implemented purely via MAIN-world DOM inspection with the existing 16 page actions unchanged and drift still a tsc error.
analysis.successDefinition: In tools/chrome-bridge the horizon is done and correct when: (1) PAGE_ACTIONS grows by one ref-addressable page-model action, added in lockstep to PageActionParams, PageActionResults, both the raw and guarded handler maps in page-actions.ts, TOOL_CATALOG and the unit-test suite, so the surface stays typed Record<PageAction,...> and any drift is a tsc error everywhere, not a runtime violation; (2) the action is implemented purely by DOM inspection inside a function injected into the page MAIN world via ports.executeScript (no chrome.debugger/CDP, no new manifest permission, no eval or (0,eval) code string), mirroring executeScript's function-injection + {world:'MAIN'} pattern that horizon 4 confirmed survives strict-CSP pages where eval does not; (3) its result is a COMPACT snapshot of actionable/interactive elements where each row carries a stable queryable ref, role, name/label and a viewport bounding box {x,y,width,height}, behind a documented predicate, a hard row cap and truncation reporting (the getPageText truncated/totalChars style) so it stays within the executeScript @1000000-char and MCP/client result-size window; (4) the snapshot is usable by the existing clickAt/hover — the center of a returned bbox feeds x/y with no intervening executeScript (the executeScript-to-get-coordinates dependency is gone for the traced path) — and the ref is re-resolvable so a selector-based typeText can still be driven from it; (5) the existing 16 page actions keep working unchanged (their contracts and handlers are unchanged), npm run verify (tsc --noEmit, eslint --max-warnings 0, vitest) is green with tests for the new action, and the MCP↔extension parity is proven by compile-time Record<PageAction,...> typing plus the two 17-count tests via `npm run verify` (the devtools:check-parity script does not exist in tools/chrome-bridge); and (6) per the binding horizon-2 decision, a horizon that changes the extension is closed only by a real-Chrome end-to-end check against a live tab proving a snapshot ref's coordinates drive a clickAt/hover there — so the final phase ends MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING until that check runs, never done-but-unverified.
assumptions: The baseline is the currently-shipped 16 page actions; PAGE_ACTIONS (actions.ts) is exactly 16 entries and PageActionParams / PageActionResults / pageActionHandlers / TOOL_CATALOG mirror it one-for-one, confirmed by reading those files, so the compaction and Record<PageAction,...> typing that makes drift a tsc error are already in place.

Adding a page action is the known ~6-place edit (PAGE_ACTIONS, PageActionParams, PageActionResults, the raw and guarded handler maps, TOOL_CATALOG, tests) recorded in discoveries.md; both the raw map and the guarded return object in page-actions.ts are typed Record<PageAction, Handler>, so a forgotten key is a compile error, and the only untyped-by-construction surface is test coverage.

The snapshot is computed by a function passed to ports.executeScript with { world: 'MAIN' } — mirroring executeScript's function-injection + {world:'MAIN'} (the only page action that already passes a world option — findElement/readPage/clickAt inject functions but run in the default ISOLATED world) — and NOT via an eval/executeScript code string, because horizon 4 established that function injection survives strict CSP while (0,eval) fails on github.com/reddit.com.

Active-tab targeting is unchanged (queryActiveTab only; no explicit tabId parameter) and top-frame only (manifest all_frames:false), so the page model walks the active tab's top-frame DOM and the existing tab-targeting model is a deferred feature.

No new manifest permission is required: the snapshot is achievable with the current [tabs, activeTab, scripting, storage, alarms] permissions plus <all_urls> host_permissions, and the content_scripts already inject a MAIN-world page-script.js at document_start that coexists with a per-call executeScript.

Bounding box is in viewport coordinates (getBoundingClientRect clientX/Y, CSS pixels from the top-left of the viewport), consistent with clickAt/hover's x/y (elementFromPoint, COORDINATE_PROPERTIES) — a box center can therefore be passed directly to clickAt(x,y).

"Actionable/interactive element" is a defensible heuristic: an element with an explicit role/aria role, an interactive ARIA role, a semantic interactive tag (button, a[href], input, textarea, select, option, etc.), a tabindex >= 0, or contenteditable. The exact predicate is an implementation detail this horizon must pick and document, not leave vague.

"Stable ref" is a queryable handle the snapshot produces that re-resolves to the same element on the current DOM — the mechanism (a CSS/nth-child path, a generated data-attribute stamp, or the array index combined with a path) is a design decision this horizon must make, choose one that is re-resolvable, and document; the index alone is not treated as sufficient because it cannot drive selector-based typeText.

The snapshot must be Compact-capable: because the DOM can be large, a defensible hard row cap and a truncation flag (truncated/totalRows style) are required so a big page cannot exceed the @1M-char executeScript boundary or the ~124KB Claude Code client window measured in horizon 4.

The horizon-2 binding decision (a real Chrome end-to-end check is required to close a horizon that changes the extension; the final phase ends blocked MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING rather than done-but-unverified) still applies to this horizon, since adding a page action changes the shipped extension.

The CDP-vs-DOM decision is NOT reopened: this horizon takes the DOM branch for the page model but leaves that decision OPEN for the future full-replacement family (gap #1), consistent with the user's explicit choice and the horizon-4 deferred list.
risks: Ref stability / re-resolvability: if the ref is a bare snapshot index, any DOM mutation or a second snapshot changes the mapping; if it is a generated CSS path, SPA class/attribute churn can break it. A ref that cannot re-resolve defeats the core objective (target the element without executeScript), so the ref mechanism must be proven re-resolvable on a live SPA DOM, not just on a static fixture.

Predicate over- or under-selection: too narrow and the element an agent actually needs (a clickable div/svg with no semantic role, a shadow-DOM user) is missing; too broad and the snapshot is not compact, blowing the @1M-char executeScript cap or the ~124KB client window. Requires a documented predicate plus a hard row cap with truncation reporting (and a live-tab size check).

Bounding-box staleness / out-of-viewport: getBoundingClientRect is viewport-relative and yields negative or off-screen coordinates for scrolled-out elements, while clickAt/hover act on elementFromPoint(x,y); a stale or out-of-viewport box center can hit no element or the wrong one. The snapshot must document boxes as viewport-relative (possibly negative) and the caller must target a visible element for the traced path.

Page-controlled result coercion: the MAIN-world function returns page-controlled data; on a malformed, non-serialisable (DOM node/function/circular), empty (elementFromPoint null / no matches), or over-large result the handler must coerce to a safe { error } sentinel — never throw and never let a raw page value cross the wire, mirroring the existing coercePointerOutcome / coerceExecuteScriptOutcome guards — otherwise a strict-CSP or JS-heavy page breaks the new action exactly the way executeScript already can.

Result-size interaction: a large DOM can produce a snapshot that exceeds the executeScript result cap or the MCP/client text block limit, so the compactness requirement is a real constraint, not cosmetic; a snapshot that must trim rows must report truncation with a total count like getPageText does, and the cap value has to be chosen defensibly this horizon.

Compile-surface edit tedium: the ~6-place edit is mechanical but spreads across protocol and extension and MCP files; the Record<PageAction,...> types catch an omitted key, but the risk is shipping the new action with a missing or weak test (the one surface the type system does not fully police) and the new action silently losing coverage, which the coverage guard would then block.

Scope creep into clickByRef / typeByRef: the traced path is feeding the snapshot's coordinates through the existing clickAt/hover, which is the stated success bar. Building a new action that internally resolves a ref and then acts (clickByRef/typeByRef) is adjacent, expands this beyond one coherent page-model capability, and is explicitly not in scope — pulling it in would violate the single-foundational-slice boundary.

Unstated CDP decision conflict: a reviewer could read this horizon as resolving the CDP-vs-DOM decision (gap #1) because it adopts a DOM page model; it does not — the page model takes the DOM branch for this slice only, and the broader CDP-vs-DOM decision stays OPEN and must not be treated as settled here.

The horizon must not silently adopt CDP/accessibility-tree semantics (e.g. Chrome's AXTree) just to make roles/names authoritative: the task explicitly says DOM-based, no chrome.debugger, no new manifest permission, so role/name are derived from DOM aria/role attributes and semantic tags, not from the CDP accessibility tree.
outOfScope: CDP / chrome.debugger adoption and any CDP accessibility-tree (AXTree) — the user explicitly chose the DOM branch for this horizon and left the CDP-vs-DOM decision OPEN, so no debugger permission or debugger session is added; role/name come from DOM attributes, not CDP.
Keyboard action(s) (pressKey / key-chord / ⌘K) — deferred gap #3; a separate capability with its own trust and focus semantics, not a part of a DOM page-model snapshot.
Scroll action / scroll-to-element — deferred gap #4; a snapshot only reports viewport coordinates of the current state; making an off-screen element reachable is a separate action.

Tab management (listTabs / open / close / switch tabs, explicit tabId targeting on every tool) — deferred gap #5; the targeting model stays active-tab-only, and tabId plumbing across protocol/relay/handlers is a separate decision and horizon.
File upload / native <input type=file> driving and upload_image — deferred medium-impact gaps gated on the CDP-vs-DOM decision; not achievable DOM-only and not in the page-model slice.
Full-page or element-clipped screenshots and screenshot format/quality options — captureTab stays viewport-only PNG; full-page capture is a separate capability and the deferred medium list.

Rich mouse / drag-drop / double/right/middle click / mouse_move sequences — beyond the existing click+hover pair; the page model only exposes coordinates to those existing actions, not new gesture families.

New clickByRef / typeByRef actions that internally resolve a ref before acting — the success bar is feeding the snapshot's coordinates through the existing clickAt/hover (and the ref to a selector-based typeText); a ref-resolving action is a separate capability and would expand this beyond one coherent slice.
Wait primitives (wait-for-selector / network-idle / implicit settle) — the bridge keeps the caller-polls model; adding wait is a separate feature not needed to return a static snapshot.
iframe / closest-frame content — the snapshot walks the top frame only (all_frames:false), matching today's all-frame model; cross-frame page modeling is a deferred gap.

Resolving the CDP-vs-DOM decision itself — this horizon takes the DOM branch for the page model but leaves the decision OPEN for the future full-replacement family; recording it as settled would fossilize an assumption (per the cliff notes on decisions.md).

The generic result-size-cap decision — this horizon may only choose a per-action snapshot row cap; the extension-side vs MCP-layer vs none result-size-cap decision stays deferred per the horizon-4 deferred list.
Any change to boky's extension, BridgeRelayModule, or extension-mcp.mjs, and any migration of boky onto the new tool — the project stays boky-free per decisions.md.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The objective is developer-tooling machinery — extending a Chrome-control extension's typed page-action surface to expose a DOM page-model snapshot for MCP terminal agents — with no business entities, rules, or workflows a domain expert would recognize, matching the project's own stated 'technical' classification in vision.md.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: The compact, ref-addressable array of actionable/interactive elements that this horizon's new action returns from the active tab's DOM.

The stable, queryable handle the snapshot attaches to each element, re-resolvable to the same element so an agent can target it (feed its bbox center to clickAt/hover, or its selector form to typeText) without executeScript.
The interactive/accessibility semantic of an element (button, link, textbox, combobox, menuitem, checkbox, radio, tab, …) derived from DOM role/aria attributes and semantic tags.
The accessible name/label of an element, derived from its text content, aria-label, aria-labelledby, alt, placeholder, or associated <label>.
The element's viewport-coordinate rectangle {x, y, width, height} in CSS pixels, computed from getBoundingClientRect, consistent with clickAt/hover's x/y coordinate model.
The subset of DOM elements the snapshot walks, selected by a documented predicate (explicit/aria role, semantic interactive tag, tabindex >= 0, contenteditable).
Running a function in the page's own JavaScript world via chrome.scripting.executeScript({world:'MAIN'}) — the snapshot's DOM inspection mechanism, which survives strict page CSP unlike (0,eval).
The existing x/y coordinate page actions that the snapshot feeds — its bbox center becomes a clickAt(x,y)/hover(x,y) call, removing the executeScript-to-get-coordinates dependency.

discoveryFindings.finding: PAGE_ACTIONS is a `as const` tuple of exactly 16 entries; PageAction is the union over it. PageActionParams and PageActionResults are each a single interface with one `readonly` field per action, and there is NO shared result envelope — every action returns its own dedicated result interface (e.g. ClickAtResult {found,dispatched}, ExecuteScriptResult {value,error?}). `Command` is a mapped type over PageAction (`params: PageActionParams[A]`), so adding a name to PAGE_ACTIONS without adding a params field is a tsc error. tsconfig has strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes all true; no-arg actions use `readonly _?: never` and results use `readonly` fields with `| null` for absent values, never optional.
discoveryFindings.implication: The new action is exactly four protocol edits: one entry in PAGE_ACTIONS, one new XxxParams interface, one new XxxResult interface, one field each in PageActionParams and PageActionResults. The result interface should use `readonly` + `| null` (not optional) for nullable fields to match house style, and the bbox/rows shape is a brand-new per-action type, not an existing envelope.

discoveryFindings.area: page-actions.ts — handler maps and guard object
discoveryFindings.finding: The raw handler map is typed `Record<PageAction, Handler>` and the guarded return object is a literal enumerating all 16 keys and is returned as `Record<PageAction, Handler>`, so a missing key in either is a tsc error. The new action must appear in BOTH the raw map and the guarded object (guarded objects wrap every non-ping handler with `guard()`, which turns throws/rejections into `{error}`).
discoveryFindings.implication: Two more edit sites in this file (raw key + guarded key), plus the action's implementation, params validation, and a page-result coercion helper. The typed Record guarantees a forgotten key fails `npm run typecheck`, exactly as the plan assumes.

discoveryFindings.area: page-actions.ts — world selection for function injection
discoveryFindings.finding: Only the `executeScript` handler passes `{ world: "MAIN" }` to ports.executeScript (line 456). findElement, getPageText, readPage, clickElement, typeText, clickAt and hover all inject their functions WITHOUT a world option, so they run in the default ISOLATED world. grep confirms `world: "MAIN"` appears in exactly one place in src/.
discoveryFindings.implication: The plan's claim that the snapshot 'mirrors findElement/readPage function injection' is right about the function-as-argument mechanism but wrong about the world: the snapshot must explicitly pass `{ world: "MAIN" }` (like executeScript does), not copy findElement's call shape. A MAIN-world-only snapshot needs that option; the DOM is also reachable from ISOLATED, so this is a correctness/design point, not a blocker.

discoveryFindings.area: page-actions.ts — result coercion and size cap
discoveryFindings.finding: Page-controlled results are coerced, never trusted: coercePointerOutcome rebuilds {found,dispatched} from primitives via `raw["found"] === true` and `asCount(...)`; coerceExecuteScriptOutcome rebuilds the executeScript envelope and applies MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS (=1_000_000) by checking `json.length` AT THE HANDLER, not inside the injected fn. The injected executeScript fn does JSON.stringify in-page and returns {ok,json} or {ok:false,error}.
discoveryFindings.implication: The snapshot needs its own coerceXxxOutcome that rebuilds an array of row primitives (ref/role/name/bbox) from `unknown` and rejects a non-record/non-array page value with an `{error}` sentinel. The size cap pattern is handler-side (coerce), but the row cap should additionally be applied IN-PAGE before returning, so a huge DOM never crosses the chrome.scripting.executeScript boundary — mirroring capture.ts's 'bound at the source' approach rather than executeScript's post-hoc JSON-length check.

discoveryFindings.finding: ChromePorts.executeScript(tabId, func, args, options?) returns Promise<unknown>; the optional `options.world` selects ISOLATED (omitted) or MAIN. The production impl delegates to chrome.scripting.executeScript({target:{tabId}, func, args:[...args], ...world}) and returns `injected[0]?.result`. queryActiveTab returns {id, windowId} for the active tab only; there is no explicit tabId parameter anywhere.
discoveryFindings.implication: No ports.ts change is needed — the snapshot is a func literal + args + {world:'MAIN'} passed through the existing executeScript. Active-tab-only, no tabId plumbing, matches the task's 'no tabId change' constraint.

discoveryFindings.finding: page-script.ts is a persistent document_start content script in the MAIN world whose sole job is wrapping console/fetch/XMLHttpRequest/uncaught-errors for capture; it builds no DOM model and exposes no reusable DOM-walk/selector/bbox helper. It is an idempotent installer driven by an injected env (for Node testability) and posts CaptureEnvelopes via window.postMessage.
discoveryFindings.implication: The snapshot must NOT reuse page-script.ts and must NOT become a new content script; it is a self-contained per-call func literal defined inside page-actions.ts (bundled into service-worker.js and serialized by chrome.scripting.executeScript at runtime), following the findElement/clickAt in-page-func style. No page-script.js change.

discoveryFindings.area: tool-catalog.ts / server.ts — catalog entry and rendering
discoveryFindings.finding: TOOL_CATALOG is typed Record<PageAction, ToolCatalogEntry> and listTools() derives the advertised set from PAGE_ACTIONS (never Object.keys). A new action needs one catalog entry: a description plus a strict inputSchema {type:'object', properties, additionalProperties:false}. server.ts handleToolCall renders every result as `JSON.stringify(response.result, null, 2)` in a single text block, except captureTab which becomes an image block; there is NO MCP-layer size cap. Stale doc headers: server.ts says 'eight page actions', tool-catalog.ts says 'Two of the ten tools', page-actions.ts says 'ten generic', types.ts says 'ten generic' — all wrong (actual 16, soon 17).
discoveryFindings.implication: One catalog entry + inputSchema (use COORDINATE_PROPERTIES / MAX_CHARS_PROPERTY style if a maxRows/limit param is added) is required; a forgotten entry is a tsc error. The stale numeric headers do not affect correctness but should be updated to 'seventeen' as part of the edit, or they will be even more misleading.

discoveryFindings.finding: listTools() derives from PAGE_ACTIONS; handleToolCall routes via isPageAction then deps.client.sendCommand(action, args); main.ts forwards action+params untyped (arguments arrive as JSON at the boundary). There is no size cap at the MCP layer (textResult just wraps the string).
discoveryFindings.implication: No dispatch change is needed — once PAGE_ACTIONS, TOOL_CATALOG and the handler maps are updated, the new tool is advertised and routed automatically. The MCP client's ~124KB window (per horizon 4) is the real constraint the row cap must serve, since the MCP layer adds no cap of its own.

discoveryFindings.area: capture.ts / capture-buffer.ts — caps and truncation pattern
discoveryFindings.finding: Existing caps: MAX_CONSOLE_TEXT_BYTES=8192, MAX_BODY_PREVIEW_BYTES=4096 (capture.ts); DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES=500, DEFAULT_READ_LIMIT=100, MAX_READ_LIMIT=500 (capture-buffer.ts). Truncation reporting patterns: boundText→{text,truncated}; CaptureRead→{entries,nextSince,dropped,truncated}; getPageText/readPage→{text|content,totalChars,truncated}.
discoveryFindings.implication: The snapshot's truncation should mirror the {rows, totalRows, truncated} shape (rows array + hard row cap + total count + truncated flag) rather than invent a new convention, and the row-cap constant should be named/exposed like MAX_READ_LIMIT so it is defensible and unit-testable.

discoveryFindings.finding: Commands reach handlers generically: bridge client onCommand → dispatch({id, action, params}) → after isPageAction check, `handlers[action](command.params)`. The dispatcher keys off the action name with no per-action case statement.
discoveryFindings.implication: Zero change to service-worker.ts or command-dispatch.ts — the new action is reachable purely by adding its key to the handler maps. Confirms the '~6-place' edit is confined to protocol + page-actions + catalog + tests.

discoveryFindings.finding: permissions are [tabs, activeTab, scripting, storage, alarms]; host_permissions <all_urls>; NO debugger permission. content_scripts has two entries, both document_start and all_frames:false — page-script.js with world:'MAIN', and capture-forwarder.js (no world field, so ISOLATED).
discoveryFindings.implication: No manifest change is required — DOM inspection via chrome.scripting.executeScript({world:'MAIN'}) is already covered by the existing scripting permission + <all_urls>. Top-frame-only (all_frames:false) matches the task's top-frame-only requirement.

discoveryFindings.finding: guards.ts narrows only frame-level shape: isCommand checks `isPageAction(value.action)` and `isRecord(value.params)` but performs NO per-action params validation (there is no clickAt/executeScript params guard). Per-action params are validated by hand inside each handler (resolveCoordinate, nonEmptyString, resolveSince, resolveReadLimit).
discoveryFindings.implication: The new action needs NO new wire guard in guards.ts; its params validation belongs in the handler (mirroring clickAt's resolveCoordinate / executeScript's isRecord+nonEmptyString). Adding a guard here would be inconsistent with the existing design.

discoveryFindings.finding: Tests use fakePorts(overrides) and fakeStore(overrides) helpers (fakeStore is a REQUIRED second arg to pageActionHandlers even for actions that ignore the store). The injected in-page function is extracted via `vi.mocked(ports.executeScript).mock.calls[0][1]` and exercised directly against `vi.stubGlobal('document', ...)` / stubGlobal('PointerEvent','MouseEvent'). The 'chrome port rejections' describe-block enumerates each non-ping handler and asserts an {error} outcome.
discoveryFindings.implication: The new action's test follows this exact pattern: a handler-level test with a canned executeScript result asserting the coerced outcome, plus an injected-fn test stubbing document.querySelectorAll / getBoundingClientRect / getAttribute to prove row building, plus adding the new action to the 'every non-ping action returns {error}' loop.

discoveryFindings.finding: Three chained passes: service-worker (ES module, emptyOutDir:true, runs first), page-script (IIFE), capture-forwarder (IIFE). page-script.ts is a separate IIFE entry only because Chrome injects manifest content scripts as classic scripts; each content-script pass sets inlineDynamicImports so shared capture.ts is inlined.
discoveryFindings.implication: NO new build entry is needed. The snapshot helper lives in page-actions.ts, which is bundled into service-worker.js as a func literal and serialized by chrome.scripting.executeScript at call time — it is not a content script, so it must not be given a content-script IIFE pass.

discoveryFindings.finding: Two unit tests hardcode the count '16' and must be edited in addition to the named 6 places: actions.unit.test.ts asserts the exact ordered tuple and `PAGE_ACTIONS.length` toBe(16); tool-catalog.unit.test.ts asserts 'advertises exactly sixteen tools' via listTools().toHaveLength(16), plus a per-action required-arguments table. There is no `devtools:check-parity` script in this package (grep finds none) — parity here is compile-time Record typing plus these count tests.
discoveryFindings.implication: The real edit is larger than '~6 places': PAGE_ACTIONS, params interface, results interface, PageActionParams field, PageActionResults field, raw handler key, guarded handler key, TOOL_CATALOG entry, the actions.unit.test.ts ordered-tuple + 16→17, the tool-catalog.unit.test.ts 16→17 (and optionally its required-args table), plus the new handler test. The plan's successDefinition mentions 'devtools:check-parity', which is a boky-side runtime script not present here — the equivalent gate in this package is `npm run verify` (tsc + eslint --max-warnings 0 + vitest) with these count tests.

discoveryFindings.finding: The stage-1.5 prompt task says each row carries a viewport bounding box `{x,y,w,h}`, while stage1-analysis.json's ubiquitousLanguage defines it as `{x, y, width, height}`. Neither 'w' nor 'width' has any existing precedent in the codebase (clickAt/hover only use x/y via COORDINATE_PROPERTIES; capture caps use byte counts).
discoveryFindings.implication: The plan must pick and document ONE bbox field convention (the analysis's {x,y,width,height} is the more self-describing and consistent with getBoundingClientRect's own .width/.height) before implementation, so the result interface, in-page fn and tests all agree — this is a latent drift risk the type system will not catch on its own.

requiredMaterials.name: Running Chromium with chrome-bridge extension loaded + relay up
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: The horizon-2 binding decision closes an extension-changing horizon only via a real-Chrome end-to-end check. The final phase (MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING) cannot execute, and the ref re-resolvable-on-a-live-SPA, predicate-breadth, and bbox-freshness proofs (the risks the analysis flags as requiring a live tab, not a static fixture) cannot be produced, without a running browser running the built extension and a reachable devtools relay.
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: cd tools/chrome-bridge && pnpm build, load dist/ unpacked at chrome://extensions, then npm start from the repo root to boot the nest-host relay (ws://localhost:8765) and drive the new action via the extension-bridge MCP ext_command. Only needed for the closing verify, not to write code; a static-fixture vitest suite cannot substitute for this.

requiredMaterials.name: Concrete target page set (live web-chat SPAs + strict-CSP/heavy-DOM pages)
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: The predicate over-/under-selection risk and the ref-stability risk must be proven on a live SPA DOM, not a static fixture. Without a concrete list of URLs to snapshot there is nothing to run the mandatory live check against, and no basis to compare against the strict-CSP pages (github.com/reddit.com) horizon 4 already proved.
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Gather the URLs the tool ultimately drives (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini chat) plus the already-tested strict-CSP pages and one heavy-DOM page; snapshot each with the new action and record role/name/predicate-match distribution to tune the predicate to not miss non-semantic clickable regions and not over-select into a non-compact output.

requiredMaterials.name: Live DOM snapshot size & interactive-element-count measurements
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: The per-action row cap and the {rows,totalRows,truncated} contract must be chosen defensibly and proven to stay under the executeScript ~@1000000-char boundary and the MCP/client ~124KB truncation window (all discovery-established budgets). Real interactive-element counts and serialized row sizes are unknown until measured on live pages; a guessed cap risks the over-selection blowout the compactness risk describes.
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Run the snapshot against each target page at a high/uncapped row cap, record the maximum interactive-element count and the serialized JSON byte size for a representative page, then set a round cap (e.g. MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS) with headroom under the @1M/~124KB budgets and document the chosen value in the tool description/catalog.

phases.name: Build page snapshot row builder
phases.goal: Add to the page-actions subsystem a self-contained MAIN-world function that walks the active tab's top-frame DOM and returns a compact, row-capped list of actionable/interactive elements, each with a stable queryable ref, role, name and a viewport bounding box {x,y,width,height}.
phases.rationale: The DOM-walk is the hard and risky core of the whole feature: it must pick a defensible interactive-element predicate, a re-resolvable ref mechanism, the bbox coordinate convention, and a hard row cap whose truncation is reported. Building and unit-testing this algorithm first, before any protocol wiring, makes that risk reviewable on its own.
changes: Add a named constant MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS (defensible round number, e.g. 500) next to MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS in page-actions.ts; it is passed to the builder as an argument, never referenced inside it, so the in-page function stays self-contained for chrome.scripting.executeScript serialization.

Add SnapshotBox {x,y,width,height}, SnapshotRow {ref, role, name, box} and SnapshotSummary {rows, totalRows, truncated} types to src/protocol/types.ts using readonly fields and | null for absent values, per the house style.

In page-actions.ts implement an exported, self-contained buildPageModel(maxRows: number): SnapshotSummary that reads the global document, walks the top frame, and returns { rows, totalRows, truncated }.

Selection predicate — include an element when it has an explicit role/ARIA role, an interactive ARIA role (link, button, checkbox, radio, tab, menuitem, combobox, textbox, option…), a semantic interactive tag (button, a[href], input, textarea, select, option), a tabindex >= 0, or is contenteditable.

For each matched element derive role from DOM role/aria attributes and semantic tags, derive name from aria-label/aria-labelledby/alt/placeholder/text/associated <label>, and compute the viewport box via getBoundingClientRect into SnapshotBox.

Attach a re-resolvable ref (a generated CSS/nth-child selector path, not a bare array index) so the same element can later be targeted by a selector-based typeText, and deduplicate so a parent and child selected by the same predicate do not both appear.

Apply the cap in-page: stop collecting at MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS rows, keep totalRows as the full matched count, and set truncated when rows were dropped, mirroring capture.ts's bound-at-the-source truncation shape.
inputs: the existing function-as-argument executeScript pattern in page-actions.ts
the capture.ts truncation shape ({entries…/totalChars,truncated} that {rows,totalRows,truncated} mirrors)
the readonly + | null protocol type convention in src/protocol/types.ts
the named-constant convention of MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS / MAX_READ_LIMIT
phases.expectedResult: An exported, unit-tested buildPageModel(maxRows) that, against a stubbed document, returns { rows, totalRows, truncated } selecting only interactive elements per the documented predicate, with ref/role/name/box{x,y,width,height} rows and an in-page-applied row cap.

rubric.label: Self-contained, serialize-able single function
rubric.ruleStatement: buildPageModel is a single top-level exported function whose body references no imported helper, no closure variable, and no module-level constant — every identifier it uses is either its `maxRows` parameter or a browser/DOM global (document, Node, Element), so chrome.scripting.executeScript can serialize it and run it in the page without a ReferenceError.
passCriteria: The deliverable declares a single `export function buildPageModel(maxRows: number): SnapshotSummary` — one top-level function literal, not an arrow returned from a factory or a curried closure.

Scanning the body, no identifier resolves to a module binding: an imported helper (e.g. `truncate`, `isRecord`, `asString`), a module-scope constant (`MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS`, `DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS`), or any local-scope variable from outside the function.
`MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS` is declared at module scope (next to `MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS`) and passed in as `maxRows`; the body never reads the constant by name.
The unit test imports `buildPageModel` from `./page-actions.js` and asserts on that exact value — the same source phase 2 injects — rather than reimplementing the DOM walk inline in the test.
A test stubs `globalThis.document` and calls `buildPageModel(10)`; it executes and returns a SnapshotSummary without throwing.
failureExamples: The developer extracts a private helper (e.g. `function interactive(el)` or `function snapshotName(el)`) to module scope and calls it from inside buildPageModel for readability. The module-scope unit test passes because the helper is in scope there, but the serialized executeScript copy throws `interactive is not defined` in the actual page.

The developer reads `MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS` (module constant) inside the body instead of using the `maxRows` argument; the module test cannot catch it because the constant is in scope in the test file, so only a live injection reveals the ReferenceError.

The function is created inside the handler factory and closes over a value computed there (e.g. `const doc = document; (maxRows) => { ...doc... }`); the closure variable is not serialized, so it is `undefined` when executed in the page.

rubric.label: Selects only interactive elements, deduped
rubric.ruleStatement: buildPageModel emits a row for each element matching the documented interactive/actionable predicate and for nothing else, and collapses a parent+child pair that both match the same predicate into a single row so the snapshot never contains duplicate subtree rows.
passCriteria: Against a stubbed document, each of these produces a row: `<button>`, `<a href="...">`, `<input>`, `<textarea>`, `<select>`, `<option>`, `<div role="button">`, `<span role="combobox">`, `<div tabindex="0">`, `<div contenteditable="true">`.

Against the same document, each of these produces no row: a plain `
`, `

`, ``, ``, `

`, `
`, `
`, `
`, `role="dialog"`, a `
`tabindex="-1"` (a negative tabindex, which removes an element from tab order) does NOT match the `tabindex >= 0` clause and produces no row.
Dedupe: a `<div tabindex="0">` that contains a `<button>` yields exactly one row, not two — a matched parent and child are not both emitted.

The predicate counts at least one of each documented clause (explicit role, interactive ARIA role, semantic interactive tag, tabindex>=0, contenteditable) as matched, i.e. it is the union described and not a narrower subset.
failureExamples: The predicate treats any `role` attribute as interactive, so a page full of `role="presentation"` / `role="heading"` / `role="list"` elements floods the snapshot with non-actionable rows; an agent clicking their bbox centers hits nothing.

The developer dedupes by the row's array index or by comparing already-built rows, so a matched parent and child both appear (or two siblings that share a ref collapse into one), leaving the subtree duplicated.

The predicate matches `tabindex="-1"` or disabled controls (e.g. treating `el.hasAttribute('tabindex')` as interactive), producing rows an agent can never actually interact with; a test that only exercises happy-path buttons stays green.

rubric.label: Refs are re-resolvable selector paths
rubric.ruleStatement: Each row's `ref` is a stable, re-resolvable CSS selector path generated from the element's DOM ancestry (a tag/nth-child chain from the root), NOT a bare array index, so a later `document.querySelector(row.ref)` resolves back to that exact element and two distinct elements never share a ref.
passCriteria: `ref` is a string selector built from the element's own tag + position in its parent (tag + nth-child or equivalent), not from the row's array position.
For every row in a fixture, `document.querySelector(row.ref)` returns the same node that produced that row (round-trip check in the test).
Every row's ref is unique across the snapshot for the fixture — no two rows resolve to the same element via `querySelector`.
Sibling elements of the same tag (e.g. two `<button>` elements in one container) get distinct refs, so a ref targets the specific element rather than the first match.
failureExamples: The developer sets `ref` to the array index (`String(i)`) because it is simpler and unique; it resolves to nothing in the DOM, so the phase-2 selector-based typeText and any `document.querySelector(ref)` return null.

The developer builds the ref from the bare tag name (e.g. `"BUTTON"`); `querySelector` returns the first button in the document, not the specific element the agent targeted, so clicks land on the wrong control.
The ref is derived from the element's id attribute when present and falls back to an index otherwise, so the dedupe or path is unstable across identical DOM structures and two elements can collide.

rubric.label: Role and accessible name derived correctly
rubric.ruleStatement: Each row carries a `role` derived from the DOM/ARIA role and semantic tag, and a `name` (accessible name) derived from the documented sources (text content, aria-label, aria-labelledby, alt, placeholder, associated `<label>`) with the correct precedence; when no name or role exists the value is `null`, never the empty string, and the protocol fields are `readonly`.
passCriteria: `<button>Save</button>` → role `"button"`, name `"Save"` (from text content).
`<input aria-label="Search">` → name `"Search"` (aria-label takes precedence over placeholder/text).
`<label for="email">Email</label><input id="email">` → the input's name is `"Email"` (resolved from the associated `<label>`), not `""`.
An element with `aria-labelledby` pointing at another node derives its name from that node's text.
An element with no derivable name (e.g. an empty `role="button"` div) yields `name: null`, and a tag with no ARIA role yields `role: null` (or the tag-derived role), never `""`.
`SnapshotBox`, `SnapshotRow`, `SnapshotSummary` fields are declared `readonly`, and `role`/`name` are typed `string | null`.
failureExamples: The developer reads `el.textContent` unconditionally and lets it win over `aria-label`, so an element a screen reader names via aria-label is mis-labelled — or, worse, `textContent` of a large container concatenates descendant text into an over-long, wrong accessible name.

The developer uses the empty string `""` for an absent name to keep the type simple, silently violating the `| null` contract so downstream `row.name ?? 'unnamed'` logic never fires for genuinely unnamed elements.
The developer resolves `alt`/`placeholder`/`aria-label` but never follows a `<label for>` by matching the element id, so for-label inputs come back unnamed even though a visible label exists.

rubric.label: Bounding box is viewport coordinates
rubric.ruleStatement: Each row's `box` is the element's viewport-coordinate rectangle from `getBoundingClientRect()` — `{ x, y, width, height }` in CSS pixels where `x`/`y` are relative to the viewport top-left — NOT `offsetLeft`/`offsetTop` (which are relative to `offsetParent`), and the box is computed in-page during the same walk.
passCriteria: Against a stubbed `getBoundingClientRect` returning `{ top: 40, left: 60, width: 200, height: 30 }`, the row's box is `{ x: 60, y: 40, width: 200, height: 30 }`.
`x`/`y` are taken from `getBoundingClientRect().left/.top` (or one rect read), never from `offsetLeft`/`offsetTop`, and never made page-absolute by adding `window.scrollX`/`scrollY`.
All four fields are always present as numbers; an element with a zero-size box still emits `0`s rather than `undefined` or omitted keys.
`box` is computed inside the injected function (same pass that reads `document`), not rebuilt or adjusted on the extension side after the executeScript returns.
failureExamples: The developer uses `element.offsetTop` / `offsetLeft` (offset coordinates relative to the offsetParent, not the viewport), so after any scroll the snapshot's coordinates are off and clickAt/hover act on the wrong spot.

The developer calls `getBoundingClientRect()` and returns the rect directly but never guards the zero-size case, so a hidden-but-matched element contributes `{width:0,height:0}` and the agent's center math (x+width/2) produces an in-bounds but empty click.
The developer records `box` on the extension side by re-querying after injection, so it reflects a different scroll position than the one the walk captured.

rubric.label: In-page row cap with reported truncation
rubric.ruleStatement: The row cap is applied inside buildPageModel: it stops collecting at `maxRows` rather than slicing afterward, returns the full number of matches as `totalRows`, and sets `truncated: true` only when rows were dropped — mirroring the `{ ..., totalChars, truncated }` shape used by the capture readers.
passCriteria: A fixture with N > maxRows interactive elements returns `rows.length === maxRows`, `totalRows === N`, and `truncated === true`.
A fixture with exactly maxRows interactive elements returns `rows.length === maxRows` and `truncated === false` (equal-to-cap is not truncation, matching capture-buffer.ts).
A fixture with fewer than maxRows returns `rows.length === totalRows` and `truncated === false`.
`totalRows` is the true full matched count (all matches, not the capped value), so a caller can always see how many elements were omitted.
The function stops pushing past `maxRows` during the walk (cap applied in-page) rather than collecting everything and `.slice(0, maxRows)` at the end.
failureExamples: The developer collects every match and only slices `.slice(0, maxRows)` at the end, then computes `totalRows` from the capped array, so `totalRows` is the row count instead of the true match count.

The developer sets `truncated` from `totalRows > maxRows` where `totalRows` was already the capped count, so a page with exactly 500 interactive elements reports `truncated: true` when it should be `false`.
The developer treats `rows.length === maxRows` as equivalent to truncation, so a page that happens to hit the cap exactly is reported as truncated even though nothing was dropped.

phases.healerHint: Keep buildPageModel a single self-contained function that reads only `document` and its `maxRows` argument — any imported helper, closure variable, or the MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS constant referenced inside it will be undefined when executeScript serializes the function into the page, so unit-test that exact exported function against a stubbed document rather than extracting private helpers at module scope.

phases.name: Add page-model snapshot action
phases.goal: Add the pageModel page action to the whole typed surface of the page-actions subsystem so it compiles and is advertised as the 17th MCP tool, and implement the extension-world handler that runs buildPageModel with { world: 'MAIN' } via ports.executeScript and coerces the page-controlled result into a safe shape.
phases.rationale: The surface is one atomic, compile- and test-forced unit: PAGE_ACTIONS, PageActionParams/Results, the raw and guarded handler maps, and TOOL_CATALOG are all typed Record<PageAction,…>, so a forgotten key is a tsc error, and the two hardcoded-16 count tests must move to 17 or the suite fails. The handler, its coercion guard, and the catalog entry must therefore land together.
changes: Add 'pageModel' to PAGE_ACTIONS in src/protocol/actions.ts, add a PageModelParams { _?: never } interface and a PageModelResult (pageModel-specific variant of SnapshotSummary) to types.ts, and add the pageModel field to both PageActionParams and PageActionResults.

Add a coerceSnapshotOutcome(raw: unknown) helper in page-actions.ts that rebuilds each row's primitives from unknown, rejects a non-record/non-array page value with an { error } sentinel, and never lets a raw DOM node/function/circular page value cross the wire.

Implement the 'pageModel' handler: validate params, resolve the active tab via ports.queryActiveTab(), call ports.executeScript(tab.id, buildPageModel, [MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS], { world: 'MAIN' }), and return coerceSnapshotOutcome(raw). Only the executeScript handler passes { world: 'MAIN' } today, so mirror that call shape.
Add the 'pageModel' key to both the raw Record<PageAction, Handler> map and the guarded return object (wrapped in guard()).

Add the TOOL_CATALOG 'pageModel' entry — a description plus a strict no-args inputSchema (additionalProperties: false, properties: {}) — and update the stale header counts in tool-catalog.ts / types.ts / page-actions.ts / server.ts from 'ten' or 'sixteen' to 'seventeen'.

Update actions.unit.test.ts (ordered tuple + toBe(16) → 17) and tool-catalog.unit.test.ts ('advertises exactly sixteen tools' → seventeen, plus the per-action required-args table), add 'pageModel' to the 'every non-ping action returns { error }' loop, and add a handler-level test asserting { world: 'MAIN' } is passed and a canned result is coerced.
inputs: buildPageModel and the SnapshotRow/SnapshotSummary types from the preceding phase
the typed Record<PageAction,…> surfaces: PAGE_ACTIONS, PageActionParams/Results, the raw and guarded handler maps, and TOOL_CATALOG
the guard() wrapper and the coercePointerOutcome / coerceExecuteScriptOutcome coercion helpers
the two hardcoded-16 count tests and the fakePorts/fakeStore test helpers
phases.expectedResult: The pageModel page action is live: the 17th MCP tool, type-driven by the Record<PageAction,…> surfaces, whose handler returns a coerced { rows, totalRows, truncated } snapshot from the active tab via a MAIN-world injection, with all count tests and the new handler test green.

rubric.label: pageModel is wired through every Record surface
rubric.ruleStatement: Adding 'pageModel' must leave every compile-time Record<PageAction,...> surface consistent, so a green `npm run typecheck` is the minimum proof of full wiring; the tool must also be advertised with the same strict no-args schema as ping/captureTab.
passCriteria: `npm run typecheck` exits 0 — proving PAGE_ACTIONS, PageActionParams, PageActionResults, the raw handler map, the guarded handler object, and TOOL_CATALOG all carry a pageModel member.
protocol/actions.ts adds `pageModel` to the PAGE_ACTIONS tuple (appended), and `expect(PAGE_ACTIONS.length)` is 17.
protocol/types.ts adds a `pageModel: PageModelParams` key to PageActionParams and a `pageModel: PageModelResult` key to PageActionResults.
TOOL_CATALOG.pageModel.inputSchema is the strict no-args schema `{ type: 'object', properties: {}, additionalProperties: false }` with no `required` array — identical in shape to ping and captureTab.
failureExamples: pageModel is added to PAGE_ACTIONS and TOOL_CATALOG but the `pageModel` key is missing from the guarded handler object returned by pageActionHandlers; because that object's declared return type is Record<PageAction, Handler>, `npm run typecheck` fails — green typecheck is the only proof the wiring is complete.

The pageModel catalog entry sets `type: 'object'` and `additionalProperties: false` but omits `properties: {}`, so a client may pass arbitrary keys; this compiles cleanly (the schema object is only structurally typed), so only an explicit strict-no-args assertion catches it.

rubric.label: buildPageModel is injected in the page's MAIN world
rubric.ruleStatement: The pageModel handler must call ports.executeScript with `{ world: 'MAIN' }` — mirroring the executeScript handler, NOT clickAt/hover/findElement, which run in the default ISOLATED world and cannot see page DOM.
passCriteria: The pageModel handler resolves the active tab via ports.queryActiveTab() then calls ports.executeScript(tab.id, buildPageModel, [MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS], { world: 'MAIN' }).
A handler-level unit test asserts that exact call shape: `expect(ports.executeScript).toHaveBeenCalledWith(7, expect.any(Function), [MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS], { world: 'MAIN' })`.
No pageModel call passes the options as `{}` or with `world: 'ISOLATED'`; the only executeScript call in page-actions.ts that carries a world option is the `{ world: 'MAIN' }` one.
failureExamples: The handler is written by copying the findElement call shape (`ports.executeScript(tab.id, buildPageModel, [MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS])` with no options object), so buildPageModel runs in the ISOLATED content-script world and yields nothing from the page; the typed surface and count tests stay green and only the handler test asserting `{ world: 'MAIN' }` catches it.
The MAIN world option is added only on the happy path, while a guard/fallback branch re-issues executeScript without the option, so some snapshots run in the wrong world.

rubric.label: The page-controlled result is coerced, never trusted
rubric.ruleStatement: The executeScript return value is page-controlled and may be a DOM node, a function, a circular structure, an over-large value, or a malformed envelope; coerceSnapshotOutcome must rebuild a safe shape and resolve a hostile value to an `{ error }` sentinel rather than letting it cross the wire.
passCriteria: coerceSnapshotOutcome(raw: unknown) returns `{ rows, totalRows, truncated }` for a well-formed page value and an `{ error }` sentinel for a non-object / non-array / malformed page value.

Each row's primitive fields (ref, role, name, and the bbox x/y/width/height) are rebuilt from unknown — a non-string field becomes '' and a non-finite/non-number bbox becomes a safe number (or the row is rejected/dropped) — never passed through raw.

Handler-level tests feed (a) a non-record value (undefined / null / a string), (b) a record whose `rows` is not an array, and (c) a row carrying a non-primitive field, asserting an `{ error }` sentinel or a sanitized result and never the raw page value.
failureExamples: The handler returns `{ result: raw }` trusting the page; when the page returns a DOM node or a circular object, JSON.stringify in the server throws or yields `{}`, so a valid-looking snapshot action corrupts the response — the typed surface and MAIN-world test stay green and only a coercion test against a non-record page value catches it.

coerceSnapshotOutcome rebuilds rows but copies `ref`/`role`/`name` as-is; a page that returns a number or a nested object for `role` sends a non-primitive across the wire instead of coercing it to a string.

rubric.label: Both hardcoded-16 count tests move to 17
rubric.ruleStatement: Every assertion and header comment that hardcodes the action count must move from 16 to 17, in both the tuple/count test and the catalog-length test, so the suite and wording reflect a 17th tool.
passCriteria: protocol/actions.unit.test.ts: the ordered-tuple assertion includes `pageModel`, `expect(PAGE_ACTIONS.length)` is 17, and the no-duplicates/no-extra-members block is consistent with 17.

mcp/tool-catalog.unit.test.ts: `expect(listTools()).toHaveLength(17)`, the test name reads 'advertises exactly seventeen tools', and the per-action required-args table adds a `pageModel` row expecting `[]`.

Stale counts in comments are updated: 'the ten generic page-action handlers', 'advertises exactly sixteen tools', 'Two of the ten tools', 'the only actions are the ten generic page actions', and the stale 'eight page actions' header in mcp/server.ts.
failureExamples: Only one of the two hardcoded-16 assertions is bumped: the developer sets `PAGE_ACTIONS.length` to 17 in actions.unit.test.ts but leaves `listTools()` `toHaveLength(16)` in tool-catalog.unit.test.ts, so `pnpm test` fails — the tuple member count and the catalog length are independent assertions and both must be 17.
The length is bumped to 17 but `pageModel` is missing from the ordered-tuple assertion in actions.unit.test.ts, so the 'is the exact ordered tuple' test fails even though the length passes.

rubric.label: The package gate is `npm run verify`, not devtools:check-parity
rubric.ruleStatement: The phase passes only when the real gate for this package — tsc --noEmit, eslint --max-warnings 0, and vitest, run via `npm run verify` from the repo root — is green; the devtools:check-parity script does not exist in tools/chrome-bridge and cannot substitute for it.
passCriteria: `npm run verify` from the repo root exits 0 (tsc --noEmit, eslint --max-warnings 0, vitest).
No `devtools:check-parity` command is used to claim parity; action parity is proven only by the Record<PageAction,...> typing (via tsc) plus the two 17-count tests.
failureExamples: Following CLAUDE.md, the executor runs `pnpm devtools:check-parity` expecting it to gate action parity; that script does not exist in tools/chrome-bridge, so it is skipped or fails, and parity is actually enforced only by `npm run verify`'s tsc + the count tests — a green (or absent) check-parity run proves nothing.
`npm run verify` appears green because eslint is invoked without `--max-warnings 0` in a manual run, letting a warning (e.g., a typed-but-unused helper) slip past the real gate.

phases.healerHint: When wiring pageModel, mirror the executeScript call exactly — ports.executeScript(tab.id, buildPageModel, [MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS], { world: 'MAIN' }) — and run coerceSnapshotOutcome(raw) before returning; copying the no-world call shape of clickAt/findElement, or returning raw unchecked, is the failure that stays green everywhere else.

phases.name: Test snapshot in live Chrome
phases.goal: Close the page-actions subsystem horizon per the binding rule that an extension-changing change closes only via a real-Chrome end-to-end check: build the extension, load it in a live tab, and prove a snapshot ref's bbox center drives the existing clickAt/hover and that the ref re-resolves as a selector on a live SPA DOM.
phases.rationale: A static fixture cannot prove predicate breadth, ref re-resolvability under real SPA class/attribute churn, or bbox-to-clickAt freshness — exactly the risks the analysis flags as requiring a live tab. The horizon's binding decision therefore demands this run before the work is considered done.
filesAffected: a live Chrome session driven through the extension-bridge MCP (nest-host relay on ws://localhost:8765)
target pages: github.com, reddit.com, claude.ai / ChatGPT / Gemini
changes: Run pnpm build in tools/chrome-bridge and load the unpacked dist/ at chrome://extensions; boot the nest-host relay from the repo root so the extension-bridge MCP ext_command is reachable.
Snapshot a strict-CSP page (github.com, reddit.com) and a live web-chat SPA; confirm the action returns compact rows and never an { error } sentinel on those pages.
Feed one row's bbox center into the existing clickAt/hover and confirm a real element sits under the coordinate; reuse the row's ref as a selector in a typeText call to prove re-resolvability.
Record the max interactive-element count and serialized row byte size across targets; if the default cap over- or under-selects, tune MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS and re-run the check.
inputs: the wired pageModel action (17th) from the preceding phase
a running Chrome with the built extension loaded and the nest-host relay reachable on ws://localhost:8765
strict-CSP and heavy-DOM target URLs (github.com, reddit.com, claude.ai / ChatGPT / Gemini)
the existing clickAt/hover actions to feed a bbox center into
phases.expectedResult: A real-Chrome end-to-end record proving a pageModel snapshot row's bbox center drives a clickAt/hover on a live tab and that the row's ref re-resolves as a selector for typeText, with MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS tuned against measured DOM sizes. MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING

rubric.label: Bbox center reaches the same element via clickAt/hover
rubric.ruleStatement: The recorded artifact must show that one snapshot row's bounding-box center, when fed as x/y to the existing clickAt or hover action on a live tab, lands on (or inside) the element that row describes.
passCriteria: Names the exact target URL and the specific row (ref + role + name) that is clicked.
Records the bbox {x,y,width,height} used and the computed center fed to clickAt/hover.

Shows the element actually under that center on the live tab matches the row — e.g. document.elementFromPoint(centerX, centerY) result, a screenshot, or console output confirming the event dispatched to the intended node.
Shows the click produces a real observable effect (focus, navigation, toggle) consistent with the row, not merely 'no error'.
failureExamples: Evidence asserts 'click succeeded' without ever proving the element under the center is the intended row — the bbox was read but the click's landing element was never checked.
The click was recorded on a static local HTML fixture, so the live strict-CSP/SPA requirement is unmet even though the evidence calls it a live-tab run.
The snapshot was taken, the page then scrolled or re-rendered, and the click went to a stale coordinate landing on a different element — yet the evidence still records it as a pass.

rubric.label: Row ref re-resolves to the same element as a selector after DOM churn
rubric.ruleStatement: The artifact must prove the row's ref is a re-resolvable CSS/nth-child selector (not a bare array index) and that it re-identifies the same element on the live page even after interaction or DOM churn.
passCriteria: Quotes the actual ref string and shows it is a generated selector path (e.g. a CSS/nth-child chain), not a bare array index.
Shows the ref passed to typeText (or document.querySelector) successfully resolves to an element.
Demonstrates the ref still re-resolves AFTER page interaction/re-render, not only on a freshly-taken snapshot.
Confirms the re-resolved element is the same logical node as the snapshot row (matching role/name), not a different element that merely matches the selector.
failureExamples: The 'ref' column is a snapshot array index, so re-resolving it just re-reads the array position and cannot survive DOM churn — this is not a selector.
typeText throws 'no element found' for the ref, but the evidence records it as a pass instead of surfacing the failure.
The ref only resolves on the static fixture but not on the live SPA, and only the fixture case is recorded.

rubric.label: Snapshot returns compact row payloads (never an error sentinel) on strict-CSP and SPA targets
rubric.ruleStatement: The artifact must record that calling the snapshot action on a strict-CSP page (github.com/reddit.com) and on a live web-chat SPA returns a non-{ error }, row-capped payload whose rows each carry ref, role, name and a bbox.
passCriteria: Records the snapshot call on github.com (or reddit.com) AND on a live web-chat SPA, each returning a non-error payload.
Records the returned row count and the serialized payload byte size for each target.
Confirms every returned row carries ref, role, name, and a {x,y,width,height} bbox.
Confirms the result is row-capped (row count ≤ MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS), not unbounded.
failureExamples: The MAIN-world injection silently fails under the strict page CSP and the action returns { error }, but the evidence glosses over it and claims the page 'works'.
Only the row count is recorded; the byte size is never captured, so 'compact' and the cap decision cannot be evaluated.
Rows lack a bbox or a ref so they cannot actually be handed to clickAt, yet the artifact still calls the payload a valid page-model snapshot.

rubric.label: MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS tuned against measured DOM sizes
rubric.ruleStatement: The artifact must record the measured max interactive-element count and byte size per target, and state either the tuned MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS (with a re-run reflecting it) or an explicit justification for keeping the default.
passCriteria: Records the max interactive-element count and serialized byte size for github (or reddit) and for the SPA target.
If the default cap under- or over-selects: states the tuned value AND shows a re-run measurement at the new cap.
If the default cap is adequate: states why, citing measured counts that are all below the cap.
failureExamples: Counts are recorded but the artifact never states whether the cap is adequate or tuned — the tuning step is silently skipped.
MAX_SNAPSHOT_ROWS was changed but the measurement was not re-run, so the recorded numbers do not match the shipped constant.
The cap is justified by 'it seemed fine' with no recorded per-target measured counts.

rubric.label: Evidence recorded in documented memory and ledger left MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING
rubric.ruleStatement: The artifact must be stored where the next executor can find it (roadmap .md twin + blockers.md/discoveries.md) and the phase status must remain MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING — explicitly not closed until a human runs the real-browser check.
passCriteria: The ledger phase status reads MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING, not 'done' / 'closed' / 'verified'.
The evidence is committed to the horizon's roadmap .md twin and a note in blockers.md/discoveries.md — not only a terminal transcript or scratch file.
The artifact distinguishes what was scripted/automated from what a human must manually verify, and does not claim the manual check was run.
failureExamples: The executor marked the phase 'verified'/'closed' after an automated ext_command probe, conflating a scripted check with the mandated manual human real-browser run.
